Trip Takeaways from Pharma Companies

We met with Hengrui, Hansoh and Henlius (a Fosun Pharma subsidiary) during our China healthcare trip. Common topics included potential impacts from the new sales rep management guidelines, ASCO highlights and other key pipeline updates, and BD outlook. Below we offer our key takeaways.
Key Takeaways
Feedback on the new sales rep policies appear mixed. Innovative drugs with clear clinical value and pharma with established systems indicates limited impact.
... but some lower-tier hospitals may take time to adjust to the new sales rep registration and appointment requirements, affecting sales of some legacy drugs.
On BD, comments are largely consistent, with ongoing discussions between China and global biopharma underway, supporting unchanged or more optimistic BD target.
■ ASCO is a near-term catalyst, with most abstract release on May 21 and LBAs through May 29-Jun 2, followed by the ADA Conference in June 5-8.
The proposed ban of using China data in supporting US IND filings should not affect BD outlook in most cases under versatile global development strategies.
Hengrui (1276.HK/600276.SS)

BMS deal (note) and BD outlook: Management framed the BMS collaboration as evidence of increasing global recognition for the breadth and quality of China biopharma's innovative pipeline, including for next-gen early-stage assets. They noted that discussions expanded materially beyond the initial specific assets to broader platform technologies, and to co-development agreements for next-gen assets. The four out-licensed programs are generally close to IND-enabling stages, while the five earlier next-gen programs may take longer to move to the clinic. Hengrui also highlighted sustained biopharma interest in its pipeline portfolio, partly supported by AI-enabled drug discovery. It reiterated that the BMS deal will not affect its potential collaborations with other global biopharma companies.

Product sales and operations on track: Innovative drug sales are ramping up on track, with no hiccups in hospital entry or compliant sales activity observed. Hengrui emphasized that it has already implemented the sales rep practice guidelines with internal controls in place, and expects limited impacts. It further views the policy shift as a long-term positive, which could further differentiate drugs with proven clinical value, and benefit established biopharma with comprehensive and compliant sales management capabilities.

Overall, the data compares favorably within the emerging myosin inhibitor landscape, we believe. See our lateral read on peer data.

RAS strategy in light of rising competition: Hengrui's pan-RAS (ON) inhibitor is designed to have a balanced PK (pharmacokinetics)/PD (pharmacodynamics) profile with differentiated tissue distribution relative to peers, which is likely to lead to reduced skin exposure and lower skin rash events, pending clinical validation. Mgmt noted that some degree of rash may be inevitable with the pan-RAS class due to NRAS and HRAS inhibition. KRAS inhibitors could potentially circumvent the rash toxicity, but with the key challenge of GI tolerability and absorption. Partly due to this consideration, Hengrui's first-gen KRAS G12Di is an IV formulation, while it also has an oral KRAS G12D in Phase I and oral pan-KRAS in earlier stages. Henlius (2696.HK; a subsidiary of Fosun Pharma - 2196.HK/600196.SS)
ASCO in focus for HLX43 (PD-L1 ADC) and Serplulimab (PD-1): HLX43 (PD-L1 ADC)

update in NSCLC is a key ASCO focus. The updated Ph1/2 NSCLC data will include separate PFS data for squamous, non-squamous and EGFR wild-type and mutant subgroups, from a near-200 patient dataset and end-April cutoff date. Safety data with longer follow-up period, which had been a debate area in prior dataset, is also key to watch. Besides NSCLC, additional NPC dose-ranging data will be shown in a poster session, while GC data were deferred given limited sample size.

Global trial progress for HLX43 in NSCLC: The US Ph2 study in 2L+ EGFRwt NSCLC has enrolled >40 patients toward a ~100-patient target by August, while broader global enrollment includes >100 patients across a planned ~200-patient study. In 3L+ squamous NSCLC, particularly docetaxel-resistant patients with limited SOC, mgmt plans to discuss ORR-based endpoints with FDA around mid-year. In 2L squamous/non-squamous NSCLC, the likely registrational study design is a head-to-head trial versus docetaxel using PFS as the primary endpoint. In 1L NSCLC, company plans to explore combo with its own PD-L1/VEGF, head to head with pembrolizumab + chemo in PD-L1 TPS<50% and pembrolizumab in PD-L1 TPS>50% subgroups. Additionally, Henlius may also explore HLX43 monotherapy in 1L NSCLC. See earlier clinical trial updates for HLX43

Serplulimab entering a catalyst-rich year for global development: For Serplulimab (PD-1), peri-operative gastric cancer approval in China is expected before end-June, likely in time for NRDL negotiation, and mgmt sees potential for several hundred million RMB incremental sales in 2H26 and Rmb2-3bn peak sales domestically. US BLA submission for SCLC remains on track for mid-2026, with bridging data from ~200 patients expected at WCLC or ESMO in 2H26. Longer term, mgmt continues to see sizeable peak potential across GC, SCLC and CRC, with 1L CRC Ph3 data expected in 2027 and overall global peak potential framed at ~Rmb10bn.

Biosimilar globalization strategy: Overseas biosimilar growth remains a major strategic focus, where Henlius reiterated its target to reach US$1bn in overseas biosimilar revenue by 2030, primarily driven by the US and Japan markets where pricing and profitability remain structurally more attractive than in Europe. On the economics for biosimilar sales, mgmt indicated a ~30% revenue sharing of end-market sales on a blended basis, through both manufacturing markups and revenue sharing from its partners. Henlius will bear COGS, which shall be fairly low, while does not need to bear any sales & marketing expenses by its partner. Hence it expects most of its ~US$1bn biosimilar revenue to pass through directly into profit. Henlius also plans to pursue first-wave biosimilars for more blockbuster drugs including Keytruda, Opdivo and PCSK9 mabs in future years.

VBP and policy takes: Guidelines and timeline for the Anhui-led biosimilar VBP remains unclear at this stage. Our conversations with other industry players suggest a 2027 implementation is more likely. Separately, mgmt acknowledged near-term disruption from recent China sales rep policy tightening, particularly restrictions on hospital access in lower-tier hospitals industry wide, but believes that Henlius is relatively well positioned given it has been shifting toward more academically focused engagement, with greater emphasis on basic research collaboration.
